- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or weak (e.g., sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to recognize downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days) — model often misses immediate downward or upward corrections.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust for price pullback toward historical mean, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- When sentiment is consistently negative or shows sharp decline, model overcorrects upward — fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mid-term price stability — underestimates volatility spikes or sudden drops triggered by sentiment shifts.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model delays correction — overestimates recovery time, leading to persistent overforecasting.
- Model reacts too slowly to sentiment reversal — especially when sentiment drops below 0.3, price correction is delayed or underestimated.
